Ordinary premises are real completeness; finite-dimensional linear algebra, Gaussian elimination and Euclidean inner products; compactness of closed bounded sets and finite products; polynomial uniqueness and elementary convex secants. For lattice steps, the Euclidean algorithm and extension of a saturated subgroup to a lattice basis are explicit ordinary premises. The additional convex/polyhedral foundations are reconstructed rather than imported as named convex-analysis or density theorems.

Rational feasible density: at any REAL feasible point of a rational polyhedron, impose its active inequalities as equalities. Elimination gives a rational particular solution and rational kernel basis. Approximate the real kernel coordinates rationally; finitely many inactive positive slacks persist. This gives density in the minimal face, including boundary faces. For a real PCC, delete zero-weight endpoints and introduce perspective variables (α_j,t_j=α_jx_j). The constraints α_j≥0, Σα_j=1, A_jt_j≥b_jα_j and Σt_j∈τ, together with rational defining equations, are rational linear constraints. Feasible rational approximants eventually retain every positive weight. Their endpoints t_j/α_j and centers are rational with the original incidences. Every inherited convex cell lies in one page: otherwise its relative interior would be covered by finitely many proper affine subspaces. Multiplying their nonzero affine equations contradicts polynomial uniqueness on an open set. At any page point x, finitely many nonincident closed cells can be avoided by a neighborhood. Nearby x±u lie in incident cells. Rational feasible density in z∈τ, z±v∈σ±, z,v∈L_i gives local midpoint convexity. On a real segment subtract its chord, obtaining continuous q with zero endpoints. If q is positive internally, choose ε>0 small enough that q+εt² has an interior maximum. A sufficiently small symmetric pair there has average at least the center value plus εs², contradicting maximality. Thus each ENTIRE page is convex. No uniform local radius is assumed.

Finite full-domain convex functions are locally Lipschitz: cube vertex values bound them above; reflection bounds them below on a smaller cube; extending secants a fixed distance bounds both difference quotients. Directional derivatives are finite continuous sublinear by secant monotonicity, rescaling, local Lipschitz bounds and the convex inequality at 2tv,2tw. For a point z outside a nonempty closed convex C, a nearest point w exists by compact truncation of a minimizing sequence, and n=w−z satisfies n·(c−z)≥|n|²>0. Apply this below a full-domain epigraph and take limiting inward UNIT normals. The vertical coefficient is nonnegative and cannot be zero: full spatial projection would force the spatial coefficient zero as well, contradicting unit norm. Division gives touching affine supports and full-domain biconjugacy. A support ℓ+b touching a sublinear derivative at w has b≤0 by testing zero and b≥0 by testing 2w, hence b=0. Forms below the derivative are exactly page subgradients. Two-sided Lipschitz bounds make their closed convex sets K_i nonempty compact, and the derivative in direction v is max_{K_i}ℓ(v).

At EACH real y∈H, let K=∏K_i and let S be the ENTIRE ambient restriction image E*→∏L_i*, E=ΣL_i. S is a closed linear subspace. If K misses S, minimize |pr_{S⊥}z|² on K. For a=pr_{S⊥}z_0≠0, segment differentiation gives a·z≥|a|² on K. Represent −a by page vectors w_i. Orthogonality to every restricted ambient covector gives the ACTUAL relation Σw_i=0. Product maximization yields a strictly negative sum of directional derivatives. For small t>0, endpoints y+tw_i lie in incident cells, have equal-weight barycenter y and negative total cost. Perspective density makes this a legal real-endpoint PCC, contradicting PC. Therefore ONE ambient form supports all pages at y. Conversely, a center outside H has incident endpoint cells in its unique page, where ordinary Jensen applies. At a center in H, sum ONE common ambient support; its barycenter term cancels. Shared trace alone is insufficient.

Finite geometry: an affine dependence among more than a+1 positive hull coefficients has zero total coefficient and both signs. Subtract it up to the first zero coefficient and iterate. Thus conv(K) is the image of K^{a+1} times a compact simplex, proving compactness explicitly. Conic dependence reduction leaves independent active columns. Their finitely many inverse maps bound coefficients; a convergent sequence has a convergent representation on one subset. Hence finite cones are closed, including lineality. For an inequality cone, remove the joint homogeneous kernel as lineality. The sum of the nonnegative defining forms has a bounded section at one, since an unbounded normalized sequence would limit into the removed kernel. Add both signs of a basis of the lineality; a zero quotient needs no section. In a bounded polyhedron, move in both directions in the kernel of active constraints to endpoints gaining active rank. Boundedness supplies endpoints; rank induction terminates at finitely many vertices. Rational full-rank systems give rational vertices. Homogenization gives pointed-polyhedron vertex-hull plus recession generation: positive-height extreme rays normalize to vertices, since an affine decomposition would split the ray; zero-height rays are recession generators. The height equation makes positive-height coefficients sum to one. Fourier–Motzkin pairing and equality elimination give finite inequality descriptions and projections.

A finite LSC convex a on a compact polytope is continuous on its WHOLE domain. Vertex values bound a above by M. At x, choose a radius below every inactive slack divided by its normal norm in the affine span. Every nearby feasible direction extends to that radius while retaining all active inequalities. Convexity gives a(z)≤(1−t)a(x)+tM with t→0; LSC supplies the reverse limiting inequality. For compact-domain extended biconjugacy, strictly separate (q,t), t<a(q), below the closed epigraph. Testing (q,a(q)) in the SAME fiber forces the vertical coefficient β STRICTLY positive. Division gives affine minorants approaching a(q), including boundary points. Outside the compact domain, a spatial separator u satisfies u(q)>max_Ku, and (su)(q)−a*(su) tends to infinity because min_Ka is finite. Thus a=a** on the domain, its boundary and OUTSIDE it.

On a complete page, convex γ is the maximum of its finitely many actual affine top-cell supports. Put h=max of its actual gradients and Δ their convex hull. Constants bound γ−h. Carrier recession cones cover FULL space: along tv, an unbounded subsequence lies in one cell; divide its inequalities by t. On each such cone h is its actual cell slope. Strict positivity makes carrying cells pointed and puts zero inside Δ. Rational spatial recession rays lifted with REAL heights h(r), plus the upward ray, generate EXACT epi(h), by linearity on each cone and global sublinearity. For |f−h| bounded, φ=f* is finite bounded EXACTLY on Δ; outside, spatial separation gives divergence on a ray. It is convex LSC and therefore continuous on the WHOLE polytope. Direct maximization over generators gives F_A*=g_A on Δ and infinity outside; biconjugacy yields f≤F_A≤f+η GLOBALLY and exact appended contacts. Lower facets have positive vertical coefficient because spatial projection is full. Every lower graph face projects affinely bijectively to a hull of rational positions plus rational rays, despite irrational heights. Intersections remain genuine common faces. An unbounded normalized sequence would give a unit covector annihilating every spanning page, impossible; hence D is bounded. Common support gives nonemptiness and simultaneous Fenchel equality. For a raised convex trace f_H≤g≤f_H+η with exact recession, b=g* is continuous on WHOLE Δ_H and k−η≤b≤k. Define S_i={(r_ip,b(Tp)):p∈M} and E_i=conv(graphφ_i∪S_i)+vertical-up.
